case_name: Central Bureau of Investigation v R. S. Pai and Another
respondent:
R. S. Pai and Another
Supreme Court of India

3 April 2002
Appeal (Cr.) 1045 of 2000
The Judgment was delivered by : M. B. Shah, J.
1. Short question iswhether prosecution can produce additional documents which are gathered during investigation, after submitting charge-sheet u/s. 173 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973?
2. The Special Court (Trial of Offences Relating to Transactions in Securities) at Bombay by judgment and order dated 26 July 2000, rejected Miscellaneous Application No.338 of 2000 in Special Case No.3 of 1997 filed by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) for production of additional documents in a case where application for discharging the respondents was filed. Aggrieved by the said judgment, the CBI has preferred this appeal.
3. The prosecution story in brief is that during the period 02 April 1992 to 20 May 1992, the FIM Division, Mumbai of Syndicate Bank received funds aggregating to Rs.132.23 crores for Portfolio Managem
facts: During the period 02 April 1992 to 20 May 1992, the FIM Division, Mumbai of Syndicate Bank received funds aggregating to Rs.132.23 crores for Portfolio Management from Oil Industries Development Board, New Delhi.

It was alleged that R. Sundaresan, the then Divisional Manager of the Bank and other bank officials conspired during the above said period at Mumbai along with Directors and office bearers of M/s Fair Growth Investments Ltd. and M/s Fair Growth Financial Services Ltd and by dishonestly and fraudulently abusing their position as a public servant caused wrongful gain to private parties and corresponding loss to the Syndicate Bank.

On 02 June 1993, on the written complaint of the Chief Vigilance Officer of the Bank, case No. RC 1(BSC)/93-Mum. was registered u/s. 12 0-B read with S. 420 IPC and S. 13(2) read with S. 13(1)(d) of Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 against R. Sundaresan Divisional Manager of Syndicate Bank and K.R.N. Shenoy, Managing Director of M/s Fair Growth Investments Ltd.
After investigation, charge-sheet was filed by the CBI in the Special Court in Special Case No.3/97 at Bombay against respondent nos.1 and 2.
On 27 January 2000, respondent nos.1 and 2 filed discharge application bearing Misc. Application No.51 of 2000 and Misc. Application No.168 of 2000 before the Special Court.
issues: Whether prosecution can produce additional documents which are gathered during investigation, after submitting charge-sheet u/s. 173 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973?
petitioner_arguments: The order passed by the Special Judge is on the face of it illegal and contrary to the provisions of S. 173 (5) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

Normally the Investigating Officer is required to produce all the relevant documents at the time of submitting report, but the Investigating Officer committed mistake in not producing certain documents as in his opinion those documents were not relevant.
There was no justifiable reason to reject the application for production of additional documents.
respondent_arguments: U/s. 173 (5) Cr.P.C., the Investigating Officer has to produce all the documents at the time of submitting the report.
The order passed by the Special Court cannot be said, in any way, to be illegal or erroneous.
court_reasoning: Normally, the Investigating Officer is required to produce all the relevant documents at the time of submitting the charge-sheet.

If some mistake is committed in not producing the relevant documents at the time of submitting the report or charge-sheet, it is always open to the Investigating Officer to produce the same with the permission of the Court.
The word 'shall' used in sub-s. (5) cannot be interpreted as mandatory, but as directory.
Further investigation, if called for, is not precluded even after the charge-sheet is submitted.
holding: The appeal is allowed and the impugned judgment and order passed by the Special Court is set aside.
The application filed by the appellant for production of additional documents is allowed.
The Special Court to proceed with the matter in accordance with law.
